title: Sample project: a Monte Carlo estimate of π
text:
This post is a sample that exercises the computational pipeline behind this site: the Python cell below runs locally, Quarto freezes its output into the repository, and GitHub Actions rebuilds the site without needing Python. The code draws random points in the unit square and estimates π from the share that lands inside the quarter circle.


Code
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

rng = np.random.default_rng(2026)
n = 20_000
x, y = rng.random(n), rng.random(n)
inside = x**2 + y**2 <= 1
estimate = 4 * np.cumsum(inside) / np.arange(1, n + 1)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.8))
ax.plot(np.arange(1, n + 1), estimate, color="#2a78d6", lw=1.8)
ax.axhline(np.pi, color="#52514e", lw=1, ls="--")
ax.set_xscale("log")
ax.set_xlim(10, n)
ax.set_ylim(2.6, 3.7)
ax.set_xlabel("Number of random points")
ax.set_ylabel("Estimate of π")
ax.set_title(f"Estimate after {n:,} points: {estimate[-1]:.4f}", loc="left", color="#0b0b0b")
for side in ("top", "right"):
    ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)
ax.grid(axis="y", color="#e5e5e3", lw=0.8)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()








Figure 1: Running Monte Carlo estimate of π as more points are drawn. The dashed line marks the true value.

title: How this site is built
text:
This site is a Quarto website. The source lives in a public GitHub repository, and every push to the main branch runs a GitHub Actions workflow that renders the pages and pushes the output to the gh-pages branch, which GitHub Pages serves at supenghe.com.
Pages with code execute their Python cells only on my machine. Quarto’s freeze feature stores the results in the repository, so the build server never needs Python or Jupyter, and the published figures are exactly the ones rendered locally.
